common_name: Bronco Carex (ColorGrass Bronze New Zealand Hair Sedge)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade in spring; Bronco is part of the ColorGrass line of New Zealand sedges grown for foliage color rather than flowers.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Bronco forms loose, arching fountains of fine, warm bronzy-brown foliage, a deeper and more uniformly brown tone than the silvery curls of sibling selection Frosted Curls, giving it a rich, earthy look that pairs well with chartreuse or blue-leaved companions. It stays evergreen in mild winter climates and holds its color through the growing season with little fuss, working equally well in containers, rock gardens, or massed as a textural groundcover. Comb out old or damaged foliage by hand each spring rather than shearing, and divide congested clumps every few years to keep the mound looking fresh.

common_name: Caspian Korean Feather Reed Grass (Bronze-Tinged Salt-Tolerant Selection)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade in spring; Caspian is a vigorous selection of Korean feather reed grass noted for tolerating heat and some soil salinity better than the species.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade, where this upright, clump-forming grass tolerates prolonged summer heat and some soil salinity better than many other feather reed grass selections. Caspian carries a light bronze tinge through its green summer foliage, then produces the bottlebrush-like, pinkish-silver flower panicles typical of the species in late summer, aging to a warm tan that persists into winter. Its shade tolerance is unusual among ornamental grasses, making it a good choice for partially shaded borders where most grasses fail to flower well. Cut the clump back to a few inches above ground in late winter before new growth resumes.

common_name: Red Cloud Maiden Grass (Compact Miscanthus with Red Flower Plumes)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in average to moist, well-drained soil in full sun in spring; Red Cloud is a comparatively compact Miscanthus sinensis selection bred for abundant, strongly red-toned flower plumes.

directions: Plant in average to moist, well-drained soil in full sun. Red Cloud forms a tidy, upright-arching clump of solid green blades noticeably more compact than many maiden grass cultivars, and produces an unusually heavy crop of brilliant red flower plumes in late summer that stand well above the foliage before aging to silvery tan through fall. Its smaller stature makes it easier to place in a mid-size border than full-size Miscanthus selections, while still delivering strong seasonal color and movement. Cut the entire clump back to a few inches above ground in late winter before new shoots emerge, and divide congested clumps every several years in spring.

common_name: Blue Dart Rush (Compact Blue-Green Hard Rush)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock into consistently moist to wet soil or a shallow-water pot at a pond edge in spring; Blue Dart is a compact rush grown for its narrow, upright, blue-green foliage, marketed separately from the similar cultivar 'Blue Arrows'.

directions: Plant into consistently moist to wet soil or a submerged pot at a pond margin, in full sun to light shade. Blue Dart forms tidy, tightly upright tufts of narrow, spiky, blue-green cylindrical foliage, giving a neater and more compact presence than the straight species, and its color makes a cool contrast against the greens of other pond marginals. It tolerates shallow standing water as well as consistently moist garden soil, though it performs best where moisture never runs short. Divide congested clumps in spring and trim away any browned or damaged foliage to keep the planting tidy.

common_name: Li'l Bang Enchanted Eve Coreopsis (Dwarf Bicolor Disease-Resistant Tickseed)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Enchanted Eve is a patented dwarf member of the Li'l Bang series (PP27857) and does not come true from seed.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Enchanted Eve is a dwarf, densely branched member of the disease-resistant Li'l Bang breeding line, covering its tidy mound in bicolor daisy flowers with dark yellow petal tips shading into rich red-orange toward a golden center. Like its Li'l Bang series-mates it reaches full size in a single season, resists the foliar diseases common to older threadleaf coreopsis, and blooms heavily from early summer into fall without regular deadheading. Its compact habit suits the front of a border, edging, or a sunny container where larger coreopsis would be out of scale. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Pearl Deep Blue Carpathian Bellflower (Large-Flowered Dwarf Bluebell)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in cool, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Pearl Deep Blue is a seed strain selected for larger flowers and earlier bloom than older Campanula carpatica types.

directions: Plant in cool, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Pearl Deep Blue forms a low cushion of small, toothy green leaves that disappears each early summer beneath a heavy crop of open, upward-facing, deep violet-blue bells noticeably larger than those of the older 'Blue Clips' strain, and blooms up to three weeks earlier. Its tidy, mounding habit and extended bloom period suit rock gardens, container edges, and the front of a sunny to lightly shaded border. Deadhead spent flowers regularly to keep the display going for weeks longer, and shear the mound back lightly after the main flush to tidy the foliage.

common_name: Ascot Rainbow Spurge (Variegated Multicolor Foliage Euphorbia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring into well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun to partial shade; Ascot Rainbow (PP21401) is a patented, sterile hybrid so it will not self-sow or revert to green-leaved seedlings.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun to partial shade. Ascot Rainbow forms a compact, vase-shaped mound of blue-green foliage edged in creamy yellow through the growing season, with the variegation flushing deep red-orange once cold weather arrives, giving multi-season color beyond the chartreuse spring flower bracts typical of the genus. Its sterile hybrid origin means it holds its named characteristics reliably and will not seed around the garden like many euphorbias. Wear gloves when handling or pruning, since the milky sap is a skin and eye irritant, and cut back old flowering stems at the base after bloom to keep the mound tidy.

common_name: Little Peach Lewisia (Compact Peach-Orange Alpine Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring at a slight angle into an extremely well-drained, gritty crevice or trough in full sun; Little Peach is part of the same longipetala breeding line as 'Little Plum' and 'Little Mango', selected for soft peach-orange flower color.

directions: Plant at a slight angle in an extremely well-drained, gritty crevice, trough, or scree bed in full sun. Little Peach forms small, glossy evergreen rosettes that bloom heavily from late spring into summer with soft peach, orange, and pale yellow flowers held just above the foliage, a warmer tone than the magenta of sibling selection 'Little Plum'. Its longipetala parentage lets it tolerate somewhat more consistent moisture during the growing season than most evergreen lewisias, though sharp drainage at the crown remains essential to prevent rot. Water a bit more generously in spring than other lewisia species while still avoiding any standing moisture around the crown.

common_name: Astra Blue Balloon Flower (Compact Cornflower-Blue Platycodon)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Astra Blue is a compact seed strain selected for sturdy, self-supporting stems and an early start to bloom.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun. Astra Blue produces inflated, balloon-like buds that pop open into star-shaped, cornflower-blue flowers over a compact, sturdy mound, flowering earlier and staying noticeably shorter than older balloon flower strains so it rarely needs staking. Bloom continues for up to two months from late spring into summer, and deadheading spent flowers encourages further buds to open. Established plants emerge late in spring, so mark their location to avoid disturbing the dormant crown while weeding nearby beds, and leave the foliage in place until it yellows naturally in fall.

common_name: Heavenly Habit Jacob's Ladder (Dwarf Fern-Leaved Northern Polemonium)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in cool, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Heavenly Habit is a dwarf selection of northern Jacob's ladder with a dense, mounding habit.

directions: Plant in cool, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade. Heavenly Habit forms a dense, low mound of finely divided, fern-like blue-green foliage topped from late spring into summer with clusters of violet-blue, bell-shaped, fragrant flowers, a daintier texture than the larger-leaved garden Jacob's ladder cultivars. Its compact size and cold hardiness, drawn from an arctic and subarctic parent species, suit rock gardens, alpine troughs, and the front of a shaded border where a tidy habit matters. Keep the soil from drying out during summer heat, and divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.
